first_impression.reaction: My daughter keeps saying 'all inclusive' as if that settles it. The opening tells me straight away that food, drink, rooms and extra hours are usually quoted separately. That's the money question, so I'm reading on, top to bottom.

journey.quote: Food and drink for the reception, exclusive use, guest rooms, extra hours and outside suppliers are where packages part ways, and most venues quote them separately.
journey.reaction: Good. That's exactly the trap I was worried about. 'All inclusive' isn't, and they say so in the second sentence.

journey.section: What all inclusive means at a Greek wedding venue
journey.quote: So the honest reading of "all inclusive" in Greece is this: your stay may be inclusive, and your wedding package covers what its list names.
journey.reaction: Plain and honest. I'll be quoting this one to my husband.

journey.quote: Elounda SA states that the Municipal fee for a civil wedding and the Metropolis fee for an Orthodox wedding are not in the package rate and are charged on top.
journey.reaction: Fees on top of fees. Better to know now. This is the sort of thing a brochure leaves out.

journey.quote: Where a cell reads "Not published", the venue does not set that detail out for weddings. Ask for it in the written quote.
journey.reaction: Sensible. On the iPad the table is wide and I had to scroll sideways, but at least it tells me what to do with the blanks.

journey.quote: On the day, the list runs to two witnesses if you need them, a ceremony table with a seasonal flower display, bouquet and boutonniere, rose petals, a pre-recorded ceremony playlist, champagne while you dress, a short fireworks display and flowers and petals in your room afterwards.
journey.reaction: Bouquets, petals, fireworks. That's my daughter's department. These long lists run together on the screen and I start skimming.

journey.quote: It covers one night of accommodation on the wedding night with tailor-made amenities, a designed menu tasting for up to four guests, a dedicated in-house wedding specialist, a service team on the day, your choice of venues, premium tables, chairs and linens, Sambonet silver and Rosenthal bone china, and waterfront and garden locations for photographs.
journey.reaction: Another very long sentence of items. I'd rather this were a short list I could read at a glance.

journey.quote: The [venue policy](https://santorinigem.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/VENUE-POLICY-2027_2028.pdf) requires every couple to have a wedding planner
journey.reaction: So another person to pay on top of the venue. Glad that's spelled out, and again later in the trade-offs.

journey.quote: Ask how much is non-refundable, when each payment falls due and what happens if you postpone.
journey.reaction: Finally, deposits. This is the section I came for. The Canaves and Santorini Gem examples show the deposits are non-refundable, which is frightening but honest.

journey.quote: Santorini Gem takes a non-refundable deposit, with the rental balance due nine months before the wedding, food and drink paid 40 days before, and postponement only to the following season.
journey.reaction: Nine months before. That's a lot of money gone well ahead of the day. My husband will want to see this.

journey.quote: Ask every venue for the step-free route from arrival to ceremony, dinner and bathrooms, especially if older guests are travelling.
journey.reaction: Someone thought of Mum and her walking frame. Only one venue says anything about access, though, so we'll be asking all the others ourselves.

journey.quote: Ask which currency the contract is written in, which currency each payment is taken in, and whether card or bank fees apply.
journey.reaction: Exactly my question. It covers the currency, but not the language the contract is written in, which worries me just as much.

journey.quote: Does your travel insurance cover the wedding itself, including deposits paid to the venue?
journey.reaction: Good, insurance gets a mention. I'd have liked a word on medical cover for older guests too.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so you can [book a Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=greece-wedding-packages-all-inclusive&utm_content=primary) with your shortlist of Greek packages in hand.
journey.reaction: Australian dollars and everything in writing before we commit. That's most of what I want. A consultation sounds like I'd talk to a person.

journey.quote: When you are ready to compare your shortlist, one Wedded Advisor works with you as a single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: One person, start to finish. That's who I'd ring at 2am. Reassuring.

unanswered_questions: Which of these venues, beyond Santorini Gem, has a step-free route for a guest with a walking frame?
Will the venue contract be in English, and who reads it with us if it isn't?
Is there anything about medical care or travel insurance for elderly guests, not just the deposit?
Is the Wedded Concierge consultation a phone call with a named person before anything is paid?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am Greek time?

turn_offs_found.quote: It covers one night of accommodation on the wedding night with tailor-made amenities, a designed menu tasting for up to four guests, a dedicated in-house wedding specialist, a service team on the day, your choice of venues, premium tables, chairs and linens, Sambonet silver and Rosenthal bone china, and waterfront and garden locations for photographs.
turn_offs_found.why: Long run-on inclusion sentences like this (and the Elounda and Andronis ones) read as an unbroken block on an iPad. I lose my place and start skimming, and the practical bits get buried.

turn_offs_found.quote: | Venue and region | Package | Ceremony types | Main inclusions (short) | Charged on top or separate | Requirements or minimums |
turn_offs_found.why: Six columns with long cells is hard work on an iPad. I had to scroll sideways and squint at small text to follow one venue across the row.

would_share_with: My husband, with the deposits, currency and 'What they rarely cover' sections circled
My sister, who is looking after Mum, with the step-free access paragraph
My daughter, with the line that 'all inclusive' belongs to the holiday, not the wedding

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit
cta_reaction.why: AUD and in writing are what I need, and 'single point of contact' at the end helps. I'd click once I know the consultation is a phone call with a named person before any deposit goes anywhere.

top_3_changes: Break the long one-sentence inclusion lists (Elounda SA on the day, Four Seasons Astir Palace, Andronis) into short bullets so they read easily on an iPad.
Make the comparison table easier on a tablet, for example fewer columns or a stacked card layout on small screens.
In the quote-currency questions, add one line asking which language the contract is written in, alongside the currency.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom on an iPad)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
Title, deferred business details, sourcing and absent prices not raised as must-fix, per orchestrator
Journey types limited to the allowed enum; every turn-off has a why

open_questions.question: No blockers for this persona. Deposits, currency, fees on top and step-free access are all covered. Remaining asks are readability (long inclusion sentences, wide table on iPad) and one optional line on contract language; should-fix at most. Phone-first contact, 2am support and deposit protection are deferred business details.

assumptions: Margaret reads the whole article on an iPad because her daughter sent it, and her own mother uses a walking frame (per voice samples).
Prices are deliberately not printed, so their absence was not raised.
